text:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a p50/p99 delta on the attn hotloop after the runtime merge (runtimectl#452). p99 up ~18% on our long-tail chat workload.

deploy-bot: merged PR #452 (runtime: sampler + dynamic-batching) by mike at 2024-11-03T09:11:02Z :white_check_mark:

mike: Ack. I saw a small increase in avg in canary but thought it was noise. Do you have a perf trace?

anya: Pushed perf traces to /artifacts/attn-sampler/2209876543. Quick paste of the two runs below (before = main@r450, after = main@r452):

bench-bot: microbench summary:
```
workload: chat-long (seq=2048)
before: p50=22ms p95=68ms p99=110ms
after:  p50=25ms p95=82ms p99=130ms
delta: p99 +18% (~20ms)
```

ram: That p99 jump is notable. Any stack traces showing where the extra 20ms sits?

anya: Yep — traced kernel entry walltime. Most requests still hit flash-attn path, but there's an extra 8-30ms window in the sampler hotloop (pre-batch selection). Snippet from async trace:
```
sample_and_route() + 24ms
  -> check_kv_cache() + 3ms
  -> sampler_spin_wait() + 18ms  <-- new
  -> schedule_batcher() + 2ms
dispatch to device + 1ms
```

sarah: "sampler_spin_wait" — that was added to avoid races with the new dynamic-batching merge, but it was supposed to be lock-free/stall-free. Looks like the spin loop may be spinning longer due to a missed wake.

mike: Hmm — my change switched the sampler to use an atomic counter + futex-like wake. On fast paths we early-exit, but under load the counter flips frequently and we may be hitting a contention case where threads do a yield + nanosleep fallback. Could explain a few ms, but not ~20ms.

ram: Do we see any CPU-side context switches during the hotspot? /proc/interrupts or sched events?

anya: Yes — `perf record` shows increased context-switches in worker threads during the sampler window. Rough capture:
```
# perf stat -e context-switches,cs -p <pid>
before: context-switches: 3.2k
after:  context-switches: 27.5k
```

mike: That's huge. Maybe the sampler uses pthread_cond_timedwait fallback that calls into kernel when atomic loops exceed X tries. I set that threshold low to avoid busy-waiting on dev boxes.

sarah: Could the fused-attn kernel warmup be interacting? If sampler waits longer, KV cache prefetches may get delayed, causing more GPU stalls and longer tail. Check timeline for `kv-prefetch` RPCs.

anya: I overlaid GPU kernel timelines. In the after-run there's a 10-25ms gap between prefetch kickoff and kernel launch for several requests. When sampler_spin_wait holds up scheduling, prefetchs are still submitted but enqueue order drifts -> some kernels wait for inputs.

bench-bot: added regression label and attached perf flamegraphs at /artifacts/attn-sampler/flame-after.svg

mike: Reproduced locally with stress test. Quick hack: disabled the nanosleep fallback (i.e., pure spin until scheduled) and p99 dropped back to baseline in my local run. That's a clue.

ram: Pure spin lowered latency but increases CPU use. We need a better middle ground: adaptive backoff based on observed contention/queue length.

sarah: Also look at kernel selection path — we may be switching to a slightly different flash-attn variant under certain batch sizes due to sampler jitter. If batcher sees more fragmented requests, it may route to paged-attn variant which is slower for short prefixes.

anya: Good call. I captured batch-size distribution:
```
before: mostly 1-4 (median 2), after: more 1-2 and a higher spike at 6 due to delayed aggregation
```
That change caused ~12% of requests to hit paged-attn variant for that workload.

mike: So two compounding effects: sampler spin/futex fallback adding 10-20ms and batch fragmentation causing suboptimal kernel selection. That explains the p99 move.

ram: Let's do a micro-bisect: revert the fallback path in sampler (so spins only) and add a temporary deterministic batch-window (fixed wait 1ms) to see impact separately. Can someone run on canary?

anya: I'm running canary now with two variants: (A) fallback disabled, (B) fallback enabled + fixed batch-window=1ms. Will post numbers in ~10m.

(10m later)
anya: Results: 
```
A (no fallback): p50=23ms p95=69ms p99=112ms
B (1ms window):  p50=24ms p95=71ms p99=116ms
current (prod):   p50=25ms p95=82ms p99=130ms
```
A is almost baseline, B is intermediate. Disabling fallback recovers most of p99 but with CPU+18% on worker threads.

mike: That confirms the fallback threshold is the main culprit. I set fallback tries to 64 previously; maybe that interacts with sys-sched quantum. I can adjust to adaptive backoff: spin for X cycles, then exponential backoff but wake with a condition variable only if queue length > threshold.

sarah: Also let's add a small jitter to batcher window to avoid synchronized wake storms that fragment batches. And add a metric for "sampler_fallbacks" to alert on high counts.

ram: Agreed. Action items:
- mike: implement adaptive fallback + sampler_fallback metric (PR today)
- anya: add batcher jitter and fixed-window experiment config for canary (done)
- sarah: instrument kernel selection telemetry to report variant hit-rates per model/seq
- bench-bot: run 6h stress to verify long-tail stability

mike: I'll target a small hotfix PR that sets fallback disabled by default (opt-in) and adaptive backoff behind a flag. Will include local microbench numbers.

anya: Sounds good. If bench-bot shows no regressions under 6h, we can push revert to rollback the fallback earlier.

bench-bot: scheduled 6h stress on canary cluster, artifacts at /artifacts/attn-sampler/2209876543/stress-6h

ram: One last note — check for any accidental NVTX markers inserted in the sampler path (I saw NVTX spans in traces) — they can change profiling and scheduling behavior under CUDA. If present, make them conditional on debug flag.

mike: Will audit NVTX. Thanks for the quick triage everyone. I'll open PR and ping here when ready. :thumbsup:

anya: Thanks — great catch. Leaving tags in the perf doc for follow-ups.

mike: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/459 (draft)

anya: Closing loop: once PR is merged, let's watch p99 for 48h and consider adding automatic sampler fallback disable when p99 spike detected.

sarah: Agreed.

mike: PR opened, marking as hotfix.

bench-bot: canary stress run completed 6h: p99 variance within baseline +/-3%. No regressions observed.

anya: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll merge the fix after a brief code review.
